meta.titre: Internet and Web Browsing: browsers, URLs and how a page reaches you
meta.sous_theme: Browsers, search engines, URLs and the path of a web page

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A Form 5 student in Limbe wants past papers for revision. She opens an app on her phone, types key words and taps a link, and a page appears in seconds. Behind this simple action are a browser, a search engine, a web address and a web server. The GCE tests these words directly, for example by asking which software opens web pages or what interprets HTML. Learn who does which job and you will not lose marks to confusion.

items: A network is a group of computers connected so that they can share data.
A file has a name and a type, and a web page is stored in a file.
Typing key words into a box is a way of telling the computer what to look for.

sections.titre: Internet and web browsing: browsers, URLs and how a page reaches you
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Internet and World Wide Web

The **Internet** is the worldwide network of connected computer networks. The **World Wide Web** (the Web) is one service that runs on the Internet: a huge collection of linked web pages stored on web servers. Other Internet services include email and file transfer. An **ISP** (Internet Service Provider) is the company that gives a user access to the Internet.

### Web pages and browsers

A web page is a text file written in **HTML** (HyperText Markup Language). A **web browser** is the software that requests a web page, **interprets** its HTML tags and displays the result. Examples are Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari and Opera. A browser is not the same as a **search engine**: a search engine is a website, such as Google or Bing, that finds pages matching key words.

### Reading a URL

A **URL** (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a page. For `https://www.example.cm/news/today.html` the parts are:

| Part | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol | `https` | The set of rules used to transfer the page; the s means the connection is encrypted |
| Domain name | `www.example.cm` | The name of the web server |
| Path | `/news/today.html` | The folder and file on that server |

### What happens when a page is opened

1. The user types a URL or clicks a **hyperlink** (a link to another page).
2. The domain name is converted into the numeric address of the server (its IP address) by a DNS server.
3. The browser sends a request to the web server.
4. The server sends back the HTML file.
5. The browser interprets the HTML and shows the page.

### Browser tools

The **address bar** holds the URL, **tabs** keep several pages open, **back** and **forward** move through pages, **refresh** reloads a page, a **bookmark** (favourite) saves an address and the **history** lists the pages already visited.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks which software opens web pages
variantes.contenu_markdown: The program that opens and displays pages is the **browser**. A search engine is only a website that you open with the browser to look for other pages. If the question says the software interprets HTML, the answer is the browser, never the web server or the search engine.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question gives an address and asks for its parts
variantes.contenu_markdown: Split the address at its separators. The text before `://` is the protocol, the text up to the next slash is the domain name, and what follows is the path to the file. In `http://www.shopexample.cm/shoes/index.html` the protocol is `http`, the domain name is `www.shopexample.cm` and the path is `/shoes/index.html`.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to compare or explain
variantes.contenu_markdown: The Internet is the global network (the hardware and connections). The Web is a service on that network made of web pages. Email is another service on the Internet and does not depend on the Web.

sections.enonce_markdown: A student types `https://www.collegexample.cm/results/form5.html` into the address bar. (a) Name the software she is using. (b) Identify the protocol, the domain name and the path. (c) Describe in order what happens until the page is shown. (d) Explain why she sees a formatted page and not raw tags.

etapes.justification: Software that requests and displays web pages is a browser.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) A **web browser**, such as Chrome or Firefox.

etapes.justification: The address is divided at `://` and at the slashes.
The server must be found first, then asked for the file, then the file is displayed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (c) The domain name is converted to an IP address by DNS, the browser sends a request to the web server, the server sends the HTML file, and the browser displays it.

etapes.justification: HTML is text with tags that give instructions.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (d) The browser **interprets** the HTML tags, so it shows headings, paragraphs and links instead of the tags themselves.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The student uses a web browser. The URL has protocol https, domain name www.collegexample.cm and path /results/form5.html. The browser requests the page from the server and interprets the HTML to display it.

items.pourquoi_faux: Google (the search page) is a website that finds other pages. Chrome and Firefox are browsers.
items.correction_markdown: Use a **browser** to open a **search engine**.

items.erreur_markdown: The Internet and the World Wide Web are the same thing.
items.pourquoi_faux: The Internet is the network; the Web is one service that uses it. Email is on the Internet but is not part of the Web.
items.correction_markdown: The Web is a **service** on the Internet.

items.erreur_markdown: HTML is interpreted by the search engine.
items.pourquoi_faux: A search engine only finds pages. The browser reads the tags and shows the page.
items.correction_markdown: HTML is interpreted by the **web browser**.

items.erreur_markdown: An ISP is a company that makes web pages.
items.pourquoi_faux: An ISP provides access to the Internet. Web pages are stored on web servers by their owners.
items.correction_markdown: ISP: **Internet Service Provider**, which gives access.

items.erreur_markdown: A page that starts with https is always true and safe.
items.pourquoi_faux: The s means that the connection is encrypted. It says nothing about whether the content is honest.
items.correction_markdown: https protects the **connection**; judge the content separately.

items.enonce_markdown: Which of the following are web browsers: Firefox, Bing, Safari, Wikipedia?
items.solution_markdown: **Firefox and Safari** are web browsers. Bing is a search engine and Wikipedia is a website.

items.enonce_markdown: A data bundle of 500 MB costs 1,000 FCFA, and one web page uses 2 MB. How many pages can be opened with the bundle, and what is the cost of each page? Also name the protocol and the path in `http://www.shopexample.cm/shoes/index.html`.
items.solution_markdown:
Pages = 500 $\div$ 2 = **250 pages**.

Cost per page = 1,000 $\div$ 250 = **4 FCFA**.

Protocol: **http**. Path: **/shoes/index.html**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web, give two Internet services other than the Web, and name two browser features that help a user return to a page later.
items.solution_markdown:
The **Internet** is the worldwide network of connected networks. The **World Wide Web** is a service on it, made of linked web pages stored on web servers and displayed by browsers.

Other services: **email** and **file transfer**.

Features: **bookmarks (favourites)** save the address of a page; the **history** lists pages already visited. Tabs also keep pages open.

items_markdown: The Internet is the global network; the Web is a service on it made of linked pages.
A browser requests and interprets HTML to display pages; a search engine is a website that finds pages.
A URL has a protocol, a domain name and a path.
An ISP provides access to the Internet; a DNS server converts a domain name into an IP address.
Useful browser tools are the address bar, tabs, back and forward, refresh, bookmarks and history.
